claims.claim: The proposal requests 420,000 ADA plus a 105,000 ADA contingency reserve to fund a part-time maintainer for Oura over 12 months at an annual rate of $105,000 USD.
The total requested withdrawal is 540,750 ADA, consisting of 525,000 ADA for Oura Maintenance and Enhancement and a 15,750 ADA Intersect Budget Administration fee.
Oura is a Rust-native pipeline tool that connects to Cardano nodes, monitors blockchain events, and routes matching patterns to pluggable outputs for processing.
Oura supports multiple data sources including N2C, N2N, S3, Mithril, and UTxO RPC, and supports sinks including Kafka, Elasticsearch, AWS services, RabbitMQ, Redis, SQL databases, and webhooks.
Oura has 654 commits, 288 stars, 79 forks, and 58 contributors, and is described as the most starred project in the TxPipe portfolio.
Oura has been funded twice through Project Catalyst in Fund 9 and Fund 13 for feature development.
The proposal achieved the required 67% support threshold during the 2026 Intersect Budget Process Hydra Voting phase.
The requested amount does not at submission breach the 350M ADA Net Change Limit covering Epoch 613 to Epoch 713, either alone or in aggregate.
Independent oversight is said to be provided through Intersect and technically capable third parties, with reporting obligations and milestone-based disbursement controls.

TxPipe has received funding through 30 Project Catalyst proposals across Funds 9 through 14, with 26 delivered and 4 under development and on schedule, and also received 2025 Intersect maintenance funding for Pallas, Dolos, and UTxO RPC that is being delivered on schedule.

summary: The document requests 540,750 ADA for 12 months of Oura maintenance, community support, AI-oriented documentation, and administration, with claims of ecosystem utility, prior funding history, Intersect budget-process approval, NCL compliance, and smart-contract-based oversight.
